URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/30/somali-pirates-killed-five-crew-members-on-hijacked-tanker-officials-say
Al Jazeera (bylined Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and Reuters) — "Somali pirates killed five crew members on hijacked tanker, officials say". Published 30 September 2026. CONFIRMED 30 Sep publication; the EVENT (the killings and the recovery operation) was Tuesday 29 September and was announced by Puntland on Tuesday.
Retrieved via WebFetch. Facts and quotes as returned by the tool.

VESSEL: MT Honour 25, Palau-flagged oil tanker.
HIJACKED: 21 April 2026, off Somalia. Cargo 18,500 barrels of oil.
DEATHS: 5 crew killed — 3 Pakistani nationals, 1 Myanmar national, 1 Indian national.
INJURED: 4 crew — 3 Pakistani, 1 Indian.
PIRATES CAPTURED: 16 suspected pirates.
SIGNIFICANCE (as stated by the article): first pirate killings in over a decade off Somalia's coast.

OFFICIALS NAMED:
- Mohamed Abdulkadir Salah — Puntland Minister of Fisheries and Marine Resources
- Mohamed Mubarak — head of Puntland's security coordination office

DIRECT QUOTES (verbatim as returned):
Puntland Information Ministry statement: "Before the operation began, the pirates on board the ship killed five of the crew."
Minister Mohamed Abdulkadir Salah: "With this operation by the PMPF, we have demonstrated that we have the ability to do so, and we will."
India's embassy in Kenya: "deeply saddened by the killing of the Indian crew member."

FROM THE SAME ARTICLE (via Exa snippet of the Al Jazeera copy, cross-checked):
"MOGADISHU, Somalia - Pirates have killed five crew members on board a Palau-flagged oil tanker off the coast of Somalia before security forces rescued the ship, according to Somali authorities."
"The Information Ministry of Puntland, a Federal State in northeastern Somalia, said in a statement that a rescue mission had freed the ship and captured 16 suspected pirates."
Puntland Maritime Police Force, in a post on social media: the vessel was "safe" and under the government's control; efforts were continuing to find others involved in the hijacking.

CAUTION — CONTESTED SEQUENCE (do NOT state as settled):
Puntland says the five were killed BEFORE its forces boarded. Surviving Pakistani crew, via the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust, told Pakistan's Express Tribune the sailors were shot by retreating pirates DURING the operation. Express Tribune / Somalia Today / Ship Universe are NOT approved domains, so only the Puntland account above is citable. The precise circumstances are not independently established.
